newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: European Commission's key WTO objectives.
newsitem.headline: European Commission's key WTO objectives.

text.p: The following is a statement from the European Union's Commissioner for Trade Policy, Sir Leon Brittan, about the European Commission's key objectives for this week's World Trade Organisation (WTO) ministerial meeting.
"Broadening the work programme of the WTO to cover new issues where future trade obstacles are likely to arise, such as investment and competition policy;
Building a consensus on removing barriers to trade in information technology products and preparing the ground for an amitious world deal on basis telecommunications services.
"Bringing the least developed countires closer to the benefits of world trade liberalisation;
Relaunching in earnest the negotiations towards Chinese membership of the WTO."
As to whether the work begun at Singapore will lead to the creation of a new trade round, Sir Leon said in his statement:

"A work programme does not prejudge any possible future decision to move to negotiations. This will be for us all to take freely, later: there can be no coercion in WTO. But this week's decisions should make it possible for us to launch in due course the future broad-based round of talks, which could properly be called the Millennium Round that I personally believe can start by the end of the century."
